clue.text: Held out with excuse, ditching former lover? That's the plan

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
ditching means dropping, so the letters for a past partner leave the word excuse

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Someone held out with an excuse and dumped an old flame, and that was the plan all along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching' takes EX from EXCUSE, leaving CUSE; 'out' then shuffles HELD and CUSE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable or programme of intended events is a plan, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Court about to animate heartless defendant, in lawyer's view

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the court abbreviation goes round the other piece
heartless means the central letter of the word is removed

parts.note: to liven is to animate or enliven

explanation.surface: A courtroom scene in which a lawyer tries to rouse a listless defendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like the setting but only supplies its abbreviation; 'heartless' removes the central letter of the animating verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To a lawyer, the person they represent, such as a defendant, is a client.

clue.text: Takes down American military set-ups

parts.note: bases are military installations

explanation.surface: US forces dismantle their military installations.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone down a peg is to humble or degrade them, the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: No introduction of an extra burden

indicators.note: no introduction means the word loses its opening letter

parts.note: a bonus is an extra payment or reward

explanation.surface: A complaint that an extra charge should not be brought in as a further burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No introduction of' removes the first letter B from BONUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A responsibility or obligation laid on someone is a burden, the core sense of the word.

clue.text: A drink's about to be sold? Pretty much

indicators.note: about means going around, so the drinks surround the auction word

parts.note: a soda is a drink, and the possessive is read as SODAS
at an auction a lot is going, going, gone, so to go is to be sold

explanation.surface: A fizzy drink is about to be put up for sale, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: At auction a lot is 'going', so 'to be sold' is GO; the possessive 's is read as a plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means virtually or nearly, as in 'as good as finished', the idiom for almost.

clue.text: Magician supporting whirling ropes

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting

indicators.note: whirling suggests spinning about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A conjuror's helper, perhaps, backing up a rope trick with spinning cords.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whirling' signals the anagram of the rope word. The puzzle has a Tempest theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Prospero is the exiled duke and sorcerer at the heart of Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Sitting up, disregarding one source of sibilant sounds

indicators.note: disregarding means leaving out, so one letter is dropped
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a sitting of a court or parliament is a session

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter, and one copy of it is removed

explanation.surface: Sitting upright while ignoring one hissing noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses SESSION to NOISSES; 'disregarding' removes one S, the first letter of 'sibilant'.
explanation.definitionFit: Noises are sounds, especially loud or unwanted ones, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Monster caught early Saint, getting one imprisoned

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: imprisoned means held inside, so the numeral is locked within the saint

parts.note: St Alban was the first recorded British Christian martyr
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A monster is captured by an early saint who gets one locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside ALBAN to give ALIBAN after C.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliban is the savage, misshapen slave in The Tempest, often called a monster in the play.

clue.text: Early curtailment of angry argument producing sadness

indicators.note: curtailment means losing the tail, done early in the clue to the first word

parts.note: sore can mean angry or aggrieved, especially in American usage
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: Cutting short an angry argument early leaves only sadness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early curtailment of' cuts the last letter from SORE to leave SOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrow is deep grief or distress, a stronger synonym of unhappiness.

clue.text: Cut back, restricting first of local celebrations

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the reversed word holds the letter
back means the word is turned round and read in reverse

parts.note: to sever is to cut

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Local festivities are cut back and limited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns SEVER into REVES; 'restricting' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Revels are lively festivities or merrymaking, a plural synonym for parties.

clue.text: Director to do well around timeless film locations?

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the success word wraps the other piece

parts.note: to score is to succeed or do well

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: sets are where scenes of a film are shot

explanation.surface: A film-maker succeeding by shooting in sets that look ageless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeless' means minus T, the usual abbreviation for time; 'around' wraps the result in the success word.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the American film-maker behind Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.

clue.text: Set out, drifting into small piece of Pacific?

definitions.text: Set out, drifting into small piece of Pacific?

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the shuffled letters enter the pair

parts.note: a small piece of the word Pacific is its first two letters

indicators.note: drifting means moving aimlessly, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A boat sets out and drifts into a tiny corner of the Pacific Ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' makes UTTOSE, which goes 'into' the first two letters of Pacific. The whole clue doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave harbour on a voyage is to set out on the ocean, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Almost everyone swallowing drop of rum (that is, a spirit)

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the shortened word holds the rest
almost means not quite complete, so the final letter goes

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: a drop is a tiny amount, here the opening letter

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, meaning that is

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone downs a drop of rum, which is, after all, a spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' seems to continue the rum surface, but it is the definition: a sprite, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ariel is the airy sprite who serves Prospero in The Tempest, a supernatural being.

clue.text: Stops losing time over middle of day? That's smart

indicators.note: the piece is laid over the centre of the word, replacing its middle letter
losing means a letter is shed from the word

parts.note: rests are pauses or stops

explanation.surface: Someone stops and loses time around midday, but at least looks smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes T from RESTS to give RESS, which covers the middle letter A of DAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy describes clothes that are formal and elegant, a sense of smart.

clue.text: Shocking weather circles Metro with added bit of tension, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way
a bit of a word here is its first letter

explanation.surface: Lightning-filled weather surrounds a city metro and adds to the tension.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange CIRCLES, METRO and T, the first letter of 'tension'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderstorm with lightning is weather that is literally shocking, a playful description.

clue.text: Duty to involve Queen in military operation

indicators.note: involve means take in, so the tax word wraps round the royal letters

parts.note: excise is a duty or tax on goods
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A soldier's duty may include the Queen in a military manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: A military exercise is a training manoeuvre or operation carried out by troops.

clue.text: Water and mop would do for this parasite

indicators.note: would do for means could be turned into, so the letters are remade

explanation.surface: Water and a mop would be enough to get rid of this pest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapeworm is a flat intestinal worm living off its host, a classic parasite.

clue.text: Shops cut short pleasant experience leading to harm

indicators.note: cut short means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a mall is a set of shops under one roof
a treat is a pleasant experience

explanation.surface: Shopping trips cut short turn a treat into something harmful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shops' gives a single shopping centre; 'cut short' lops its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To maltreat is to treat cruelly or injure, a verb synonym of harm.

clue.text: Dozing snake seen around shelter

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the snake encloses the shelter

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A sleeping snake is seen curled round a shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dozing means lightly sleeping, so the two describe the same state.

clue.text: Come up to rabbit on about river

indicators.note: about means around, so the talking word goes round the river letter

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for chattering, as is to spout

explanation.surface: Someone comes along only to talk endlessly about a river.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'rabbit on' is British slang for talking at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To sprout is to come up out of the ground, as seedlings do.

clue.text: Odd bits of life completely evident in end of sea journey

parts.note: the first and third letters of life are L and F, written out as a phrase
all means completely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: Signs of life become obvious when a ship reaches shore at last.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd letters of 'life' are spelt out in words as 'L and F', giving LANDF.
explanation.definitionFit: Landfall is the arrival at or first sighting of land after a voyage at sea.

clue.text: Note male abandoning responsible character

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter is left behind, swapped for the other

parts.note: a mature person is responsible and sensible

explanation.surface: A note about a male walking out on a dependable personality.
explanation.walkthrough: N takes the place of M in MATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's nature is their essential temperament or personality.

clue.text: Beds? Fine hoaxes seeing removal of head

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: removal of head means the opening letter is taken away

parts.note: put-ons are hoaxes or deceptions

explanation.surface: Nice beds, but they turn out to be pranks once the top is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: A put-on is a hoax; 'removal of head' takes away its first letter. F for fine is familiar from pencil grades.
explanation.definitionFit: Futons are Japanese-style mattresses that serve as beds.

clue.text: Grain worldwide initially involved in standard economic competition

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so the pieces go within the standard

parts.note: par is a standard or norm
rice is a cereal grain

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

explanation.surface: Grain sold around the world gets drawn into a fight over prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A price war is rivalry where firms keep undercutting each other's charges.

clue.text: Incline to batter front of portcullis

parts.note: to ram is to batter or strike forcefully

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers prepare to batter down the portcullis at the castle gate.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramp is a sloping surface, so it is a noun synonym of incline.

clue.text: Trainers with disapproving comments about soldiers

indicators.note: about means around, so the disapproving noises enclose the soldiers

parts.note: tuts are clicks of disapproval
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Coaches tut disapprovingly at their soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutors are teachers or coaches, people who train others.

clue.text: Treasurer's hoarse whisper about it

indicators.note: about means around, so the rough sound goes round the appeal letters

parts.note: a burr is a rough, whirring or rasping sound
it is slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: The finance officer hoarsely whispers about something.
explanation.walkthrough: BURR goes round SA; 'it' meaning sex appeal is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursar manages the finances of a college or school, a kind of treasurer.

clue.text: Care about artist — a magician's daughter

indicators.note: about means around, so the care word wraps the artist

parts.note: to mind is to care, as in 'I don't mind'
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist and the daughter of a conjuror who cares.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist; Prospero is the magician of The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is Prospero's daughter in The Tempest, and Prospero is a sorcerer.
